case_name: Sunil Kumar, S/O Mr Krishna Kumar vs Dr. Chanchal Pal, D/O Ramendra Pal

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sunil Kumar, aged about 42 Years, S/o Mr. Krishna Kumar
parties.respondent_defendant: Dr. Chanchal Pal, aged about 43 Years, D/o Ramendra Pal

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a writ petition against an order passed by the Family Court on October 10, 2019. The respondent had filed a petition for divorce under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, claiming desertion. Petitioner contended that the marriage was hit by Section 15 of the Act and hence not valid.

legal_principles.principle: Maintainability of a petition/plaint at the time of issuance of notice has to be seen in the light of averments made in it only.
legal_principles.held: It is trite law that maintainability of a petition/plaint at the time of issuance of notice has to be seen in the light of averments made in it only.
cited_cases: Sunil Kumar, S/O Mr Krishna Kumar vs Dr. Chanchal Pal, D/O Ramendra Pal (2020)

legal_principles.principle: One can be permitted to assail the order issuing notice by placing altogether new/fresh material before this Court in the writ petition.
legal_principles.held: He is at liberty to raise his objection before the learned Family Court by placing the appropriate material to substantiate his objection;
cited_cases: Sunil Kumar, S/O Mr Krishna Kumar vs Dr. Chanchal Pal, D/O Ramendra Pal (2020)

use_for_drafting: filing a writ petition in the High Court
